paper.title: Online Learning for Equilibrium Pricing in Markets under Incomplete Information

unmapped: Equilibrium pricing: operator posts a price p in [0,1]; n suppliers with private increasing, mu-strongly convex cost functions best-respond with production; operator observes total production (revealed preference feedback), not the losses
Three regret metrics measured simultaneously: unmet demand, cost regret, payment regret (relative to equilibrium price)
Cost functions and demand fixed over all periods; responses are deterministic
settings.definition_quote: As a warm-up, we first consider the setting when the cost functions of the suppliers and customer demand are fixed over the $T$ periods. Formally, the supplier cost functions satisfy $c_{it}(\cdot) = c_{it'}(\cdot)$ for all $t, t' \in [T]$ and the demands satisfy $d_t = d_{t'}$

settings.name_in_paper: Fixed cost functions and time-varying demand
unmapped: Equilibrium pricing with posted prices in [0,1] and strongly convex private supplier costs; operator observes total production
Demand d_t in [d_lower, d_upper] varies arbitrarily over time and is observed before pricing (acts as context)
The learner knows the demand interval [d_lower, d_upper] (used for discretization)
Three regret metrics: unmet demand, cost regret, payment regret
settings.definition_quote: we suppose that the customer demands for the commodity are time-varying and lie in a continuous but bounded interval, i.e., the customer demand at each period $t$ is some variable quantity $d_t \in [\underline{d}, \overline{d}]$.

settings.name_in_paper: Time-varying cost functions (i.i.d., no contexts) (lower bound)
unmapped: Supplier cost functions drawn i.i.d. each period from a distribution known to the operator; realizations unobserved
Benchmark is the per-period equilibrium price for the realized cost function
Three regret metrics: unmet demand, cost regret, payment regret
settings.definition_quote: There exists an instance with fixed time-invariant demand and a single supplier whose cost functions are drawn i.i.d. from some (potentially known) distribution

unmapped: Cost function c_i(.; phi_i, theta_it) with private time-invariant phi_i and observed time-varying context theta_it; contexts and demands arbitrary sequences
Learner uses an online regression oracle for the class F mapping (price, context) to production
Cost functions mu-strongly convex and l-Lipschitz smooth
Three regret metrics: unmet demand, cost regret, payment regret (in expectation over randomized prices)
settings.definition_quote: the cost function of each supplier $i$ is parameterized as follows: $c_{it}(\cdot) = c_i(\cdot; \phi_i, \theta_{it})$, where $\phi_i$ is private information and $\theta_{it}$ is the time-varying component of the cost function given to the operator as contexts.

settings.name_in_paper: Fixed convex (not strongly convex) cost functions (lower bound)
unmapped: Supplier cost functions convex but arbitrarily close to linear (strong convexity constant can tend to 0)
Three regret metrics: unmet demand, cost regret, payment regret
settings.definition_quote: There exists a class of convex supplier cost functions for which no online algorithm can achieve sub-linear regret on all three performance metrics.

source.label: thm:IdenticalResult
source.quote: The unmet demand, cost regret, and payment regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:fixed-demand-constant-reg} are $O(1)$ if the cost functions of the suppliers are strongly convex.

results.notes: Bound holds simultaneously for unmet demand, cost regret and payment regret (deterministic). Proof shows sum |p_t - p*| <= 1, times constant max{L0,L1,L2}.

conditions: supplier cost functions strongly convex and increasing
demand d_t in a known bounded interval [d_lower, d_upper]

source.label: thm:VaryingDemandResult-sqrtT
source.quote: The unmet demand, cost regret, and payment regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:time-varying-demand-new-sqrt} are $O(\sqrt{T})$ if the cost functions of the suppliers are strongly convex.

results.notes: Bound applies to each of the three metrics; algorithm does not need T (doubling epochs).

bound.expression_latex: \text{no sub-linear regret on all three metrics}
bound.regime: in the limit of strong convexity alpha -> 0

conditions: single supplier with cost c(x) = alpha/2 x^2 + beta x, alpha -> 0
statement: at least one of the three metrics is not sublinear (payment regret O(1/alpha) unbounded or unmet demand linear)

source.label: prop:impossibility-strongconvex
source.quote: There exists a class of convex supplier cost functions for which no online algorithm can achieve sub-linear regret on all three performance metrics.

results.notes: Qualitative impossibility; recorded as Omega(T) on the max of the three metrics, which is an interpretation.

conditions: single supplier, demand d=1, cost c1(x)=x^2/8 or c2(x)=x^2/16 each w.p. 0.5 i.i.d.; distribution known, draws unobserved
bound is on the expected sum of unmet demand, payment regret and cost regret

source.label: prop:time-varying-cost-countereg
source.quote: There exists an instance with fixed time-invariant demand and a single supplier whose cost functions are drawn i.i.d. from some (potentially known) distribution such that no online algorithm can achieve sub-linear regret on all three regret metrics.

results.notes: Constant 7/64 from the proof in Appendix C.1; lower bound on total (sum of three metrics) expected regret.

conditions: single supplier, demand d=1, cost x^2/6 or x^2/12 + x/4 each w.p. 0.5 i.i.d.; distribution known, draws unobserved
bound on expected sum of relaxed (aggregate) unmet demand, payment regret and cost regret

source.label: prop:time-varying-cost-countereg-2
source.quote: There exists an instance with fixed time-invariant demand and a single supplier whose cost functions are drawn i.i.d. from some (potentially known) distribution such that no online algorithm can achieve sub-linear regret on payment regret, cost regret, and the relaxed unmet demand metric

results.notes: Constant 1/96 from proof in Appendix C.2 (per-period expected total regret at least 1/96).

source.label: thm:igw-bound-informal
source.quote: With high probability, for any sequence of contexts $\theta_t$ and customer demands $d_t$ over $T$ periods, the unmet demand, payment regret, and cost regret satisfy: $\EE_{p_t \sim \Delta_t, t \in [T]}[U_T(p_1, \dots, p_T)] \le O\left(\sqrt{KT \cdot \est(T)} + \frac{T}{K}\right)$

results.notes: Informal theorem; expectation over algorithm's randomization, high probability over history. Same bound for P_T and C_T. Proposition 4 states the same bound on the proxy regret.

symbols.Est_T: regret bound Est_sq(T) of the online regression oracle

conditions: cost functions mu-strongly convex and l-Lipschitz smooth

source.label: thm:igw-bound-informal
source.quote: If we choose $K = \sqrt[3]{T / \est(T)}$, then we have $\EE_{p_t \sim \Delta_t, t \in [T]}[U_T(p_1, \dots, p_T)] \le O\left(T^{2/3} \cdot \sqrt[3]{\est(T)}\right)$.

results.notes: For finite F (Remark 3) Est(T)=log|F| giving O(T^{2/3} log|F|^{1/3}). Appendix gives further instantiations (linear class, Lipschitz, neural nets).

symbols.Est_T: online regression oracle regret bound Est_sq(T)
symbols.eps_mis: misspecification level of F w.r.t. true production function

conditions: F is eps-misspecified w.r.t. suppliers' optimal production
cost functions mu-strongly convex and l-Lipschitz smooth
any sequence of contexts and demands
tuning: gamma = sqrt(K T / (Est(T) + eps^2 T + log(1/delta)))

source.label: thm:main-contextual
source.quote: If the function class $\mathcal{F}$ is $\varepsilon$-miss-specified with respect to the suppliers' optimal production $x^*(p_t; \theta_t)$, then with probability $1-\delta$, and for any sequence of contexts $\theta_t$ and demands $d_t$, Algorithm~\ref{alg:time-varying-cost} achieves the following bound on our regret metrics: ... \lesssim \sqrt{KT \cdot \est(T)} + \varepsilon \sqrt{K} \cdot T + \frac{T}{K} + \sqrt{KT \log(1/\delta)}

results.notes: Same bound in Theorem 4 for the proxy regret. Applies to U_T, P_T, C_T (expected over price randomization).
